feat(crabbox): protect cloud setup secrets through egress (#171073)

Cloud setup used to forward host environment values through plaintext `setupEnv`, which disabled automatic snapshots and prepared workers. `settings.setupSecrets` replaces it: up to 16 POSIX environment names mapped to protected shared-store SecretRefs. One job-scoped egress owner gives profile setup, recipe preparation and postCreate/postStart commands only sentinels plus public CA trust; Crabbox native egress keeps the authenticated upstream proxy on the Gateway host, allows public HTTPS package downloads, and substitutes each secret only for its store-bound destinations. Grants revoke before process termination on cancellation.

Devcontainer `secrets` requests resolve only through the operator-approved map; unmapped requests fail once, before repository commands run. Setup secrets no longer disable snapshots or prepared workers; images captured with protected egress use a distinct compatibility identity, so older plaintext images are never adopted.

Requirements: an owned coordinator Linux lease and Crabbox 0.77.0 or newer with its matching runtime helper. Unsupported targets, a missing helper or login, an unavailable proxy, missing bindings and old CLIs fail visibly; there is no plaintext or direct-egress fallback.

Update behavior: the Crabbox plugin's Doctor health repair migrates each `setupEnv` profile atomically, and only when every same-name protected store entry already has destination bindings and there is no conflicting host value or mapping. It writes through Doctor's backed-up config writer, never writes store values, never invents destinations, and stays lazy when no profile needs migration. Unrepaired profiles report a remedy (`openclaw doctor --fix`) instead of forwarding plaintext. No SQLite schema change.

Merged with main after #170929 (empty-workspace cloud sessions): empty workspaces still require project-preparation support, so they stay cold on setup-command-only providers.

fix: tool call text no longer leaks into chat output when provider chunks split a call marker (#169172)

* fix(tool-call-repair): keep call text private when chunks split a call marker

A buffered tail that is still an unfinished call marker ("<funct", "<|channel|>")
was replayed as a false-positive prefix when a complete call preceded it, so the
rest of the call arrived mid-buffer and was emitted as visible text. Hold the
buffer while the tail can still complete into a call, replay only decided
false-positive prefixes, and route trim bookkeeping through one helper so the
done/error/EOF paths share the same chunk-independent decision.

Regression tests cover a replayed false prefix, a stacked function call, and a
stacked Harmony call split across chunks.

Refs #169161

* fix(tool-call-repair): align split-stream replay with the block origin

The split-marker buffering added in the previous commit diverged from the
unsplit stream when an authoritative text_end extended the same content block
("hello\n[read]\n{}\nX\n  " lost the call placeholder). Classify
delta-path buffers with the same finalize context as snapshots, keep the block
offset when a text_end extends a buffered snapshot, and track per-content-index
consumed input length so non-authoritative replays slice from the right origin.

Adds three regression tests (plain text and Harmony, delta and text_end split
shapes); stream-normalizer suite 58/58 and packages/tool-call-repair +
normalization-core 445/445 pass, fuzz seed=1 20k iters failures 71 -> 56 and
leakToSplit 18 -> 10 versus the previous commit.

Refs #169161

* chore(tool-call-repair): store the touched files with LF line endings

The previous uploads kept a CRLF final newline captured from the local
working copy; the repository stores these files as LF, so the PR diff
picked up a spurious trailing-line change on both files. No code changes.

Refs #169161

* style(tool-call-repair): format the new test cases with oxfmt

check-lint failed on the previous commit because the three added it.each
rows exceeded the formatter width; run oxfmt's default formatting on the
test file (source file already clean). No behavior change.

Refs #169161

* fix(tool-call-repair): keep trim replay order and drain buffered aux

Replays each false-positive prefix segment with its own content block template and unit accounting instead of the latest template, and interleaves the replayed text with queued reasoning in arrival order. Every trim path (delta, done, error, queue overflow, EOF) now drains buffered auxiliary events before clearing the candidate queue. Adds regression tests for the three review repros.

* test(tool-call-repair): cover terminal trim drains for done, error, and queue cap

* fix(tool-call-repair): keep trimmed snapshot offsets local to their block

A trim can drop earlier content blocks whole, so the retained suffix can
start inside a later block. Advancing snapshotOffset by the concatenated
buffer's removed length made authoritative text_end reconciliation slice
at the wrong origin: the f865603 review repro ('[read]' then
'x\n<function=read>' plus text_end) leaked 'ion=read></function>' as
visible text.

Derive the new origin from the original part that contains the retained
suffix so replay slicing and cumulative snapshots agree, and add the
cross-block cumulative-snapshot case to the block-index regression.

* refactor(tool-call-repair): isolate bounded stream suppression

Keep the stream coordinator below its inherited line budget by moving the existing oversized-payload state machine into a sibling module. Preserve the shared grammar and request tool allowlist, and strengthen marker-split regressions with independent visible-text expectations.

* fix(pr-wrapper): list the extracted suppression module in the wrapper inventory

6caf20c moved the bounded stream suppression state machine into packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer-suppression.ts, but scripts/pr only extracts scripts/pr, scripts/pr-lib, and the paths listed in wrapper-components.txt. Without the entry the extracted anchor cannot resolve ./stream-normalizer-suppression.js, so eager-import-closure fails on the PR wrapper inventory and on the extracted dependency context.

fix(skills): keep background reviews out of user reply hooks (#171651)

## What Problem This Solves

Detached Skill Workshop reviews inherit the foreground user trigger, so user-only reply hooks can mistake background maintenance for a new user turn.

## User Impact

Background learning no longer starts user-only reply hooks such as Advisor. Foreground user turns remain eligible; the review's model, tools, source snapshot, and permission checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review is admitted as system work but reuses the foreground prompt context. Clear its inherited trigger at the producer so every hook sees the correct distinction, rather than adding session-key exclusions to individual plugins. The trigger taxonomy has no generic system-maintenance value, so this run leaves the optional trigger unset.

## Evidence

- Production experience-review regression proves a user-eligible claiming hook handles the foreground turn, then does not dispatch for the detached review through the real review forwarding and reply-hook dispatcher; review model work proceeds.
- 33 focused tests passed: experience review (9), review scheduler (12), and reply-hook boundaries (12).
- Scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` passed.
- Madge import-cycle check: 0 cycles.
- Documented that background reviews are internal system work, not user turns.

fix(codex): project raw outer tool-call lifecycles (#171661)

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex harness projects native app-server items (`commandExecution`, `dynamicToolCall`, and so on) to the `codex_app_server.item` agent-event stream with `started`/`completed` phases. Outer model tool calls that Codex records as raw response items have no projected lifecycle: function calls, custom tool calls (for example the code-mode JS `exec` wrapper), local shell calls and tool-search calls. A plugin that must know whether any tool call is still running therefore sees the run as idle while an outer code-mode call is still open, because its child shell commands have already completed.

This was found live with the Advisor plugin (#169564). It must not fork a session while a call is still open, because codex-rs normalization then fabricates an `aborted` output for the open call.

## Fix

`handleRawResponseItemCompleted` now also projects raw call receipts as `codex_app_server.item` `{ phase: "started", itemId: call_id, type }`, and their recorded outputs as `{ phase: "completed", itemId: call_id, type }`. Only phase, id and type are copied, never arguments or results. The app-server forwards raw response items after codex-rs records them in history, so `completed` means the output is persisted. Call and output receipts share `call_id` (codex-rs `protocol/src/models.rs`).

## User Impact

None by itself. Plugins that track in-flight work on Codex runs (with `payload: "metadata"`) can now see outer tool calls start and finish. The existing subscriber (`run-attempt.steering-settlement`) is unaffected.

## Evidence

- Projector test: raw function, custom, local-shell and tool-search calls produce paired started/completed events with ids and types only.
- The steering-settlement subscriber tests still pass.
- Live (Advisor, Codex runtime): before this change, a review boundary was reached while the outer code-mode call was open, and the Gateway logged a missing custom-tool output. Advisor's regression, an outer call open while its children are complete, holds the review until the outer output is recorded.

fix(ai): turns fail without compaction when Hugging Face TGI rejects an over-long prompt (#158161)

* fix(ai): reject exhausted proxy completions budgets in every thinking mode

When the estimated input leaves no room for output, the openai-completions
request builder falls back to max_completion_tokens=1 and still sends the
request. #157673 turned that into a context overflow for thinking-enabled
reasoning models; non-reasoning models and thinking-off requests still send
the one-token request, which cannot hold a useful reply and comes back cut
off by length.

Throw the same context_length_exceeded error for those requests when the
estimate leaves zero or negative output space, so the existing overflow
recovery compacts instead. Positive short budgets (1-15 tokens that fit the
estimate) and their insufficient_output_budget warning are unchanged for
non-reasoning and thinking-off requests, and deliberately short requested
budgets are untouched.

Refs #157307

* fix(ai): budget exhausted non-thinking proxy requests without the estimate margin

The openai-completions request builder estimates input as chars/4 with a
1.25 safety margin. Against a real tokenizer (Qwen3) that estimate is
1.4-1.6x the true count for prose, code, tool schemas and CJK text, so a
fixed prompt that really fills about 65-73% of the context was refused
before provider I/O, with nothing for compaction to recover.

When the margined estimate leaves no room and thinking is off (or the
model is non-reasoning), budget from the unmargined chars/4 estimate
instead and refuse only when that also leaves no room. If the unmargined
estimate undercounts, the provider's own context-length rejection enters
the same overflow recovery. Thinking-enabled requests keep the margined
estimate and the 16-token floor from #157673.

The runtime's required-maintenance test now passes unchanged: its
foreground requests go out with roughly 700 and 4,400 output tokens
instead of triggering an extra overflow compaction. The refusal fixtures move to estimates of at
least 1.25x the context, and an explicit one-token request at an
exhausted estimate is still sent.

* fix(ai): hold proxy completions caps to the useful floor on both estimates

The unmargined fallback only fired once the margined estimate left no room
at all, so a non-thinking request whose margined room was 1-15 tokens was
still sent with that cap (down to 1, the original one-token defect), and
the cap then jumped back up once the margin was fully exhausted.

For requests without thinking, budget from the unmargined estimate as soon
as the margined estimate leaves fewer than 16 output tokens, and refuse
with context_length_exceeded when the unmargined room is also under 16.
Every cap that context pressure reduces is now at least 16 tokens, caps
fall steadily within each estimate, and refusal is terminal as the prompt
grows. Thinking-enabled requests keep the margined estimate and the
16-token floor from #157673 unchanged. A caller's own maxTokens that fits
the room (1, 2, 16) is still sent as requested; only budgets that context
pressure cuts are held to the floor.

The refusal now says which estimate it used and how many of the 16
tokens remain, instead of "leaves only 1 output tokens" for an exhausted
prompt. The margin drop is logged as keep_max_tokens when a caller's cap
is honored without clamping, and the insufficient_output_budget warning
is removed because no reduced cap under the floor is sent any more.

* fix(ai): warn when proxy completions fall back to the unmargined estimate

Budgets taken from the unmargined estimate were logged only at debug
level, so the warn-level signal operators used to spot prompts at the
context cap (the insufficient_output_budget lines) disappeared by
default. Log those clamp_max_tokens and keep_max_tokens lines at warn
level, with the margined estimate alongside, since the provider may
still reject the request. Ordinary clamping stays at debug level.

Document the requested-cap rule exactly: the room never counts below one
token, so a requested cap of 1 is sent in every mode even when the
estimate already exceeds the context, and a prompt that really does is
rejected by the provider and enters overflow recovery. Any other

## Problem

Meta Muse Code needed terminal setup: `muse login`, `openclaw plugins enable muse`, and a hand-written `agentRuntime: { id: "muse" }` on the Meta model. Model Setup offered only "Meta: API key". Other subscription logins (xAI, GitHub Copilot, OpenAI Codex) already work from the Models page.

## Solution

- **Meta provider owns a "Muse Code" device-code choice** (`extensions/meta/muse-login.ts`). It runs `muse login` under supervision, shows the device code in the wizard, honors cancel, and gives an install hint when `muse` is missing. The Gateway login always uses Muse's file credential store under `<stateDir>/muse`, so one browser approval is enough. The macOS Keychain write fails for background Gateway processes.
- **The credential stays Muse-owned.** No fake OpenClaw profile is written. The muse harness uses the managed credential when present and otherwise falls back to Muse's own store. Model availability uses the harness's existing catalog/readiness hooks over the same authenticated MSP `model/list`; it does not grant the direct Meta Responses route.
- **Setup installs and routes the runtime.** `runtime-plugin-install.ts` gains a Muse descriptor beside Codex and Copilot. The auth result enables `muse` and returns an `agentRuntimeId: "muse"` hint; setup writes it only to the activated agent's model entry (`agents.entries.<agent>.models[<model>]`). Global `agents.defaults.models` rows, including an explicit `openclaw` policy, and other agents are unchanged.
- **Activation verification without a tool-free turn.** Muse cannot guarantee a zero-tool turn (MSP has no all-tools-off switch), so activation's `disableTools` probe cannot pass honestly. This adds an optional, activation-only harness `verifySetup`, used only for profileless native auth. Muse checks MSP `model/list` and requires `source: "providerCatalog"` that contains the selected model. A rejected credential returns a bundled catalog and fails setup. Core binds the plugin owner/artifact fingerprints and re-runs the check before commit. Other runtimes keep the existing probe.
- **Live authority.** The `models.authLogin` setup branch carries the existing connection/choice guard through activation; an invalidated device token stops the flow before `muse login`, verification or runtime install run.
- **Catalog/UI.** The provider-login catalog marks native-setup choices `requiresSetup`. AI Setup → Connect provider lists them and dispatches through setup activation with connection-owned cancellation. The plain Provider Access list stays credential-only.

feat(sessions): run sessions in existing folders on paired devices (#169722)

Related: #136048 (non-Git directory semantics) and #142521 (non-Git worker workspace context; this PR does not implement ephemeral cloud workspaces).

## What Problem This Solves

Device-hosted sessions required a Git repository or managed worktree, a constraint inherited from ephemeral cloud sessions, even when a paired personal machine should simply work in an existing non-Git folder.

## User Impact

Users can choose **Existing folder on device** in New Session and run a session directly in an existing folder on a paired session-host device. OpenClaw does not create Git metadata, copy the folder to the Gateway, or sync, reconcile, reset, or delete it.

- `nodeHost.workerRuns.folders` is node-local consent: unset allows existing directories, a non-empty list restricts selection to those roots and their descendants, and `[]` disables the feature and its capability advertisement.
- The session stays pinned to that device: Auto/cloud dispatch, Move, and Continue on Gateway are refused. Attachment staging and the Gateway Files panel are unavailable for these sessions.
- Worker HOME stays in private node storage. Files are not locked against external changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `sessions.create` accepts `deviceFolder: { deviceId, path }` (requires `operator.write`); the binding is stored on the existing session entry and the `device-folder` workspace kind reuses the worker execution and lifecycle owners.
- The node owns folder policy and re-validates on every use: absolute or `~` paths only, realpath resolution (symlinks cannot escape a root), no filesystem root, no overlap with private worker storage, and a dev/ino fence between acquisition and execution. One shared rule in `node-workspace-protocol.ts` forbids preparing, resetting, transferring, seeding, or quiescing a device folder, for both ingress parsing and direct node execution.
- Gateway shutdown reads the teardown scope from the durable placement, so stopping an attachment with no in-memory tunnel no longer reaches closed worktree admission.
- A restored existing-folder create retry is owned by its frozen request; current device capacity or runtime no longer blocks it.
- Attachments are refused for device-folder sessions before anything is persisted: `chat.send` rejects them with a clear message, New Session blocks Send while attachments are attached, and worker media preparation never restages historical attachments into a device folder, so one refused file cannot make later turns fail.
- Security tradeoff: a session-host node already runs operator-directed agents with exec, so the allow-all default does not widen that boundary. The folder list is a selection guardrail, not an exec sandbox or a boundary against a compromised Gateway. Deployments that contain `operator.write` with `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` should also set a root list; the docs say so.
- Control UI selection/path input, plus docs for node configuration, session hosting, operator scopes, and workspace behavior.

## Screenshots

**After — desktop existing-folder input**

## Evidence
- **Cross-machine E2E on the final feature code:** a disposable Gateway on one Mac (tailnet TLS, token auth, QA mock model) and a session-host node on a second Mac, both on the same exact head, with `folders` unset and an existing non-Git target folder on the second Mac. Pairing and capability advertisement; create + explicit dispatch (`active`, workspace = the device folder); hosted exec wrote `pwd` and `hostname` into the folder, confirmed by independent readback on that Mac; node restart and an unclean Gateway restart, then a second turn appended to the same file; `~` and a Gateway-only path rejected; reclaim + delete left the folder, sentinel, and absence of `.git` unchanged with no copy in Gateway state.
- **Isolated single-host E2E (25 checks, all pass):** missing/root/file/relative/private-storage rejections; auto-dispatch rejection; node restarts; clean Gateway shutdown with a live tunnel and with a durable attachment but no tunnel; Gateway restart and resume; symlink escape and outside-root rejection under a root list; `[]` disables the capability.
- **Attachment refusal, live:** on the isolated Gateway, a `chat.send` with a text attachment to a device-folder session returns the refusal, the attachment never enters history, and the next text turn and later turns after node and Gateway restarts complete in the folder.
- **Authority, live (real Gateway WebSocket, no mocks):** an operator client granted only `operator.read` + `operator.sessions.write` sends `sessions.create` with `deviceFolder` and gets `FORBIDDEN` / `missingScope: operator.write`; no session row exists afterwards and a debugger logpoint on the node records no workspace command for that request. The full `operator.write` client creates and dispatches the same folder (`active`).
- **Device revocation during awaited admission, live:** with the node process tree stopped (`SIGSTOP`) while `sessions.create` and `sessions.dispatch` wait on it, `devices remove` succeeds, then `SIGCONT`. Create fails with `Selected device changed during folder validation; retry` and leaves no row; dispatch fails with `Device worker installation connection is no longer current`; the node is then disconnected and its old token is rejected. Known bounded behavior: the read-only folder validation request already delivered to the stopped node still runs once on resume (1 ms after removal) before the close frame arrives; its result is discarded, nothing is persisted, and no session command runs. Unit coverage also revokes the caller (real `captureGatewayDeviceRevocation` capture) and the device during validation.
- **Requesting-operator revocation during awaited admission, live:** separate signed operator devices with `operator.write`, real paired node stopped with `SIGSTOP`. Removing the operator while `sessions.create` waits on folder validation: the client gets `gateway closed (4001): device removed`, `sessions.describe` returns `{"session":null}`, the key is absent from `sessions.list`, and the node trace has no worker execution command. Removing a different operator while `sessions.dispatch` waits: the session moves from `provisioning` to `{"state":"failed","terminalReason":"Gateway requester authority changed"}`, `hasActiveRun` is false, and no worker command runs. As with device revocation, one already-delivered read-only folder validation runs on resume and its result is discarded.
- **Inline initial turns are refused:** `sessions.create` with `deviceFolder` plus `message`, `task` or `attachments` is rejected before node I/O; the UI already sends the first message through `sessions.send` after dispatch. The three new cases fail with the validator removed (`3 failed | 12 passed`) and pass with it (`25 passed`).
- **Upgrade compatibility, live:** the `main` merge-base build created a plain session and an explicit-cwd session (turn `ok`); the PR build on the same state dir lists and describes both with their original IDs, a new turn on the old session completes `ok`, and Doctor exits 0 with no session-row load errors.
- **Upgrade from stable `v2026.10.3`, live:** the stable build created a plain session with a completed turn, an explicit-cwd session, a custom model alias and a non-default `thinkingDefault`. Direct startup on the new build exits 78 with "uses schema version 24; … run openclaw doctor --fix" on both this PR and the plain `main` merge base (inherited). After `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (`v24 -> v26`), the PR Gateway starts, both old sessions list and describe with their original IDs, both settings read back unchanged, a new turn on the old session returns `ok`, and a new device-folder session created after the upgrade dispatches and runs a turn in the folder. One session-event publication warning about an unsettled worker-environment mutation appeared during that dispatch; the turn still succeeded.
- **Focused tests:** device-folder node, tunnel, create, protocol, media, submit-gate and draft-state suites pass; the restored-retry and history-restage regressions fail before their fixes.
- **Hosted CI:** on the exact head `364a000`, every job passes on the first attempt, and so does the Security Review, except `checks-ui-e2e (8/9)`. That job runs `plugins-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`, which also fails the same way on plain `main` (see the maintainer override comment). Earlier heads hit flaky qa-lab E2E tests and `main`-side ratchet failures that plain `main` also reproduces.

## Merge Danger

Additive optional protocol field and session-entry JSON field; no SQL schema change. Older Gateways reject the new `sessions.create` parameter; older nodes do not advertise the capability, so the option is not offered. Revert removes the feature; existing device-folder sessions would then be unrecognized but their folders are untouched.

fix(agents): keep in-flight tool calls pending in session forks (#171580)

Related: #169564

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes read-only built-in session forks reporting a still-running tool call as aborted, which can make a background reviewer recommend repeating successful work.

## User Impact

A fork taken during tool execution now describes the result as pending, not as a tool error. Parent execution and persisted results are unchanged. Ordinary `/btw` and normal-run transcript repair keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The built-in fork retains the last prepared request and appends subsequently published messages. When an assistant tool call has been published but its result has not, provider replay pairing repair inserts an error result (`aborted` for OpenAI Responses). The fork now supplies a non-error pending result only for those new, unmatched publications, before provider serialization. It keeps the actual prepared request prefix unchanged and never writes the placeholder back to the parent snapshot.

Known limitation: Codex has its own upstream missing-result repair (`codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/normalize.rs:104-107`, `CustomToolCallOutput` with `output: "aborted"`; function calls at lines 59-64). This PR does not rewrite native Codex tool outputs. Mid-call Codex forks remain subject to that upstream behavior; consumers should review at a settled boundary.

## Evidence

- Live evidence from Advisor #169564 at `1b75f3ab75f4e77a349387ef26f661e491ffa922`: six requested sequential `echo N; sleep 10` calls became ten actual executions after three false-abort corrections passed verification. All ten persisted tool results were successful. A captured verification request contained `function_call_output` with `output: "aborted"` for the still-running third call.
- Root cause: `packages/ai/src/transcript-transform.ts:154-170` synthesizes the error while replaying the fork, not in the parent's persisted transcript or its original prepared request. The assistant publication is appended by `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.ts:82-91`.
- Regression covers synchronous and asynchronous pending calls through the real OpenAI Responses and Anthropic transports, and verifies a later fork sees the genuine completed result instead of retaining the placeholder. All four cases failed before the fix for the intended missing-pending-result reason.
- Focused tests: **26 passed across 3 files** (13 fork boundary tests, 2 tool-ID preservation tests, 11 replay sanitization tests).
- Scoped TypeScript project, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks passed; `check:madge-import-cycles` reported **0 cycles**. No full typecheck, broad suite, `check-changed`, or autoreview was run.
- Live re-proof: cherry-picked onto the Advisor head as `b31c3fcf879eda6cf23c3b409b6d548571b7b78e` (local only), retaining its old tool-start scheduler. The identical six-command built-in case completed with **exactly 6 successful exec calls**. Reviews during calls 3 and 6 both returned **NO_CHANGE** (3013 ms and 1982 ms); no verification or steering occurred. Both captured fork input arrays contain the pending call's result as `This tool call is still running. Its result is not available yet.`, with no `aborted` tool output. All six genuine persisted results are successful and the parent transcript contains no pending placeholders. Gateway and isolated temporary state were cleaned up.
